title: At Umm Ma‘bad’s Tent
reader_question: What happened when the hungry travellers stopped at Umm Ma‘bad’s tent, and how did she describe her guest?

overview.text: The travellers had nothing left to eat, and it was a year of drought and hunger. On the road to Madinah they came to the two tents of Umm Ma‘bad, a woman of Khuza‘ah who gave water and food to those who passed. That day she had nothing to sell them. Her flock was out at pasture, and only one ewe was left in the tent, too weak to follow it. What happened there left a vessel of milk in her tent, and when her husband came home and asked about it, she answered him with a description of her guest that people have repeated ever since.

paragraphs.text: On the way they came to two tents belonging to Umm Ma‘bad, a woman of Khuza‘ah. Umm Ma‘bad means "mother of Ma‘bad", after her son; her own name was ‘Atikah. She was a strong woman who did not keep herself out of sight; people would come and sit with her. She sat in front of her tent with her knees drawn up, and gave water and food to those who passed. The travellers asked to buy meat and dates from her, but she had none of either.

paragraphs.text: "I saw a man of shining beauty," she said, "his face bright, his build fine. No paunch spoiled him, and no small head made him less. He was handsome and finely featured. His eyes were deep black, his lashes curved, and his voice had a slight huskiness. His neck was long, his beard thick, his eyebrows finely arched and meeting. When he was silent, dignity sat on him; when he spoke, he stood tall, and splendour came over him. From afar he was the most beautiful and splendid of people; close up, the sweetest and the finest. His speech was sweet and clear, neither too little nor too much, as if his words were beads slipping one after another from a string. He was of middle height: not so tall that he towered over others, nor so short that the eye would look down on him. A branch between two branches, he was the finest to look at of the three, and the most highly regarded."

paragraphs.text: In Makkah, Abu Bakr's family passed three nights not knowing which way he had gone. Then one of the jinn came singing up through Makkah from its lower end, with people following, hearing his voice but seeing no one, until he passed out of the upper end of the city: "May Allah, Lord of mankind, give His best reward to two companions who stopped at the two tents of Umm Ma‘bad." When they heard it, they knew he was headed for Madinah. By then the man Abu Ma‘bad meant was already gone, riding on towards Madinah.

paragraphs.text: Ibn Kathir sums it up in one line: the story of Umm Ma‘bad "is well known, transmitted through routes that strengthen one another." The words used above come from one of those routes, the report of Hubaysh ibn Khalid, which al-Hakim also recorded and declared sound, with al-Dhahabi agreeing. The modern hadith scholar Muhammad Nasir al-Din al-Albani questions that judgment for this particular chain: it passes through Hubaysh's son Hisham, whom the critic Ibn Abi Hatim lists without any praise or criticism, and with no one but his own son reporting from him. Al-Albani still allows that the report may rise to hasan (good), or even sahih (sound), through the other routes al-Hakim gives. His remarks appear as footnotes in an edition of Ibn Hajar's Hidayat al-Ruwat, added by its editor ‘Ali al-Halabi from al-Albani's notes.

paragraphs.text: The report comes down through Umm Ma‘bad's own family. Hubaysh ibn Khalid, who tells it, was her brother, and it reaches Abu Nu‘aym through his son Hisham and grandson Hizam. Ibn Hisham calls her Umm Ma‘bad bint Ka‘b, of Banu Ka‘b of Khuza‘ah; in Ibn Ishaq's report through Yunus, her name is ‘Atikah bint Khalid. Ibn Kathir, quoting al-Umawi, names her husband Aktham ibn ‘Abd al-‘Uzza and their children Ma‘bad, Nadrah and Hunaydah. Abu Nu‘aym also records a report that reached ‘Abd al-Malik ibn Wahb, without a named source, that Umm Ma‘bad later emigrated, became Muslim, and joined the Prophet ﷺ.

paragraphs.text: Ibn Ishaq tells the visit differently. In his version Umm Ma‘bad says, "By Allah, we have no food, no animal lent to us for milk, and no ewe except dry ones." The Prophet ﷺ calls for one of her ewes, passes his hand over its udder, prays, and milks into a large bowl until it froths. "Drink, Umm Ma‘bad," he says. "You drink," she replies, "you have more right to it." He hands it back, and she drinks. He then milks a second dry ewe and drinks himself, a third for the guide, and a fourth for ‘Amir. It is also Ibn Ishaq who has Quraysh reach her tent in their search, as told above.

paragraphs.text: Al-Bayhaqi records a related report from Abu Bakr himself: they came at evening to a tent standing apart in a camp, where a woman said she was alone and sent them to the chief of the camp. Her son then came home with his goats, and the Prophet ﷺ milked them for her, for Abu Bakr and for himself; afterwards she called him "the blessed one." Al-Bayhaqi thinks the two stories may be about the same woman, and suggests an order: first the ewe at the back of the tent, then her son with the goats, then her husband, to whom she described him.

paragraphs.text: Several of Umm Ma‘bad's words are rare, and the early philologist Abu ‘Ubayd al-Qasim ibn Sallam explains them. Her "neither too little nor too much" means a middle course in speech; "the eye would not look down on him" means you would not dismiss him, but welcome him and hold him in awe; "served and surrounded" means a man whose companions wait on him and gather round him. For the lashes he prefers a reading that means long rather than curved, and he describes the huskiness of the voice as slight and pleasant.

paragraphs.text: The voice in the story comes from Asma bint Abi Bakr, in Ibn Ishaq's report. Hubaysh's report in Abu Nu‘aym also goes on beyond Abu Ma‘bad's words: the next morning a voice was heard high over Makkah, and no one knew whose it was, reciting the same verses at greater length. One of its lines runs, "Ask your sister about her ewe and her vessel; if you ask the ewe, it will bear witness." In another version the voice is heard in Madinah, between heaven and earth; in the first, Hassan ibn Thabit hears it and answers with verses of his own.

source_units.text: That when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was brought out of Makkah, he left as an emigrant for Madinah with Abu Bakr, Abu Bakr’s freedman Amir ibn Fuhayrah, and their guide Abd Allah the Laythi. They passed by Umm Mabad’s two tents and asked her for meat and dates to buy, but found none with her. The party had run out of provisions (^٤) and suffered a hard year (^٥). The Messenger of Allah ﷺ then looked

source_units.text_ar: الْمُسْلِمِينَ وَإِذَا أَرَادَ التَّعَجُّبَ وَالنِّدَاءَ قَالَ: يَالِ فُلَانٍ بِالْكَسْرِ وَقَوْلُهُ: كِسَرُ الْخَيْمَةِ: هُوَ مُؤَخَّرُهَا وَفِيهِ لُغَتَانِ كِسَرِ وَكَسْرِ، وَقَالَ بَعْضُهُمُ: الْكِسَرُ هُوَ فِي مُقَدَّمِ الْخَيْمَةِ وَقَوْلُهُ: فَتَفَاجَّتْ عَلَيْهِ: يَعْنِي فَرَّجَتْ رِجْلَيْهَا كَمَا تَفْعَلُ الَّتِي تُحْلَبُ وَقَوْلُهُ: بِإِنَاءِ يَرْيِضُ الرَّهَطَ أَيْ يُنَهْنِهُهُمْ مِمَّا يَجْتَرِيهِمْ لِكَثْرَتِهِ إِذَا شَرِبُوهُ وَقَوْلُهُ: فَحَلَبَ فِيهَا ثَجًّا يَعْنِي سَيْلًا وَكَذَلِكَ كُلُّ سَيْلٍ وَمِنْهُ قَوْلُهُ ﷺ وَقَدْ سُئِلَ عَنِ الْحَجِّ فَقَالَ:
فَقَالَ مَا لَبِثَتْ إِذ جَاءَ زَوْجُهَا أَبُو مَعْبَدٍ يَسُوقُ أَعْنُزًا عِجَافًا يَتَسَاوَكْنَ هَزْلًا مُخُّهُنَّ قَلِيلٌ فَلَمَّا رَأَى أَبُو مَعْبَدٍ اللَّبَنَ عَجِبَ وَقَالَ:
source_units.text: The report says she had scarcely waited when her husband Abu Mabad came driving emaciated goats, so thin they staggered and had little marrow. When Abu Mabad saw the milk he was amazed and said:

source_units.text_ar: مِنْ أَيْنَ لَكِ هَذَا وَالشَّاةُ عَازِبٌ حَائِلٌ وَلَا حَلُوبَةَ فِي الْبَيْتِ؟
source_units.text: “Where did you get this, when the sheep are away and not pregnant, and there is no milking animal in the house?”

source_units.text_ar: فَالْعَجُّ رَفْعُ الصَّوْتِ بِالتَّلْبِيَةِ وَالثَّجُّ سَيْلُ دِمَاءِ الْهَدْيِ وَقَوْلُهُ: أَرَاضُوا: أَصْلُ هَذَا فِي صَبِّ اللَّبَنِ عَلَى اللَّبَنِ وَمَعْنَى قَوْلِهَا أَرَاضُوا: هُوَ شُرْبُ لَبَنٍ صُبَّ عَلَى لَبَنٍ وَقَوْلُهُ فَغَادَرَهُ عِنْدَهَا: يَقُولُ: تَرَكَهُ وَقَوْلُهُ: يَسُوقُ أَعْنُزًا تَسَاوَكْنَ هُزْلًا وَالتَّسَاوُكُ: الْمَشْيُ الضَّعِيفُ وَقَوْلُهُ: وَالشَّاةُ عَازِبٌ يَعْنِي قَدْ عَزِبْنَ عَنِ الْبَيْتِ فَخَرَجْنَ إِلَى الْمَرْعَى وَقَوْلُهُ: الْحِيَّلُ الَّتِي لَيْسَتْ بِحَوَامِلَ

فَدَعَا بِهَا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ فَمَسَحَ ضَرْعَهَا بِيَدِهِ وَسَمَّى اللَّهَ ﷿ وَدَعَا لَهَا فِي شَاتِهَا فَتَفَاجَّتْ عَلَيْهِ وَدَرَّتْ وَاجْتَرَّتْ فَدَعَا بِإِنَاءٍ يَرِيْضُ الرَّهَطَ فَحَلَبَ فِيهِ ثَجًّا حَتَّى عَلَاهُ الْبَهَاءُ ثُمَّ سَقَاهَا حَتَّى رَوِيَتْ وَسَقَى أَصْحَابَهُ حَتَّى رَوُوا ثُمَّ شَرِبَ آخِرُهُمْ ﷺ ثُمَّ أَرَاضَوْا ثُمَّ حَلَبَ ثَانِيًا بَعْدَ بَدْءٍ حَتَّى مَلَأَ الْإِنَاءَ ثُمَّ غَادَرَهُ عِنْدَهَا وَبَايَعَهَا ثُمَّ ارْتَحَلُوا عَنْهَا
source_units.text: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ had it brought, stroked its udder with his hand, named Allah ﷿ and prayed for her regarding her sheep. It spread its legs for him, gave milk, and chewed the cud. He called for a vessel that would suffice the group and milked copiously into it until foam rose over it. Then he gave her drink until she had enough, and his companions until they had enough; then he ﷺ drank last. Then they drank to their fill, and he milked it a second time after the first until he filled the vessel, left it with her, made a transaction with her, and they departed.

source_units.text_ar: قَالَتْ: لَا وَاللَّهِ إِلَّا أَنَّهُ مَرَّ بِنَا رَجُلٌ مُبَارَكٌ مِنْ حَالِهِ كَذَا وَكَذَا
source_units.text: She said: “No, by Allah, except that a blessed man passed by us, and such-and-such was his condition.”

source_units.text_ar: فَقَالَ: صِفِيهِ لِي يَا أُمَّ مَعْبَدٍ
source_units.text: He said: “Describe him to me, Umm Mabad.”

source_units.text_ar: وَقِصَّتُهَا مَشْهُورَةٌ مَرْوِيَّةٌ مِنْ طَرْقٍ يَشُدُّ بَعْضُهَا بَعْضًا.
source_units.text: Her story is well known, transmitted through routes that reinforce one another.

source_units.text_ar: وَاجْتَازَ فِي مُرُورِهِ عَلَى أُمِّ مَعْبَدٍ بِنْتِ كَعْبٍ مِنْ بَنِي كَعْبِ بْنِ خُزَاعَةَ، قَالَهُ ابْنُ هِشَامٍ. وَقَالَ يُونُسُ، عَنِ ابْنِ إِسْحَاقَ: اسْمُهَا عَاتِكَةُ بِنْتُ خَالِدِ بْنِ مُنْقِذِ بْنِ رَبِيعَةَ بْنِ أَصْرَمَ. وَقَالَ الْأُمَوِيُّ: هِيَ عَاتِكَةُ بِنْتُ تَبِيعٍ حَلِيفِ بَنِي مُنْقِذِ بْنِ رَبِيعَةَ بْنِ أَصْرَمَ بْنِ ضَبِيسِ بْنِ حَرَامِ بْنِ حُبْشِيَّةَ بْنِ كَعْبِ بْنِ عَمْرٍو، وَلِهَذِهِ الْمَرْأَةِ مِنَ الْوَلَدِ، مَعْبَدٌ، وَنَضْرَةٌ، وَحُنَيْدَةُ، بَنُو أَبِي مَعْبَدٍ، وَاسْمُهُ أَكْثَمُ بْنُ عَبْدِ الْعُزَّى بْنِ مُنْقِذِ بْنِ رَبِيعَةَ بْنِ أَصْرَمَ بْنِ ضَبِيسٍ،
source_units.speaker_ar: ابن كثير ينقل أقوال من سماهم
source_units.text: As he passed by, he came to Umm Ma‘bad, daughter of Ka‘b, of Banu Ka‘b ibn Khuza‘ah. This is what Ibn Hisham said. Yunus, reporting from Ibn Ishaq, said: Her name was ‘Atikah, daughter of Khalid ibn Munqidh ibn Rabi‘ah ibn Asram. Al-Um awi said: She was ‘Atikah, daughter of Tabee‘, an ally of Banu Munqidh ibn Rabi‘ah ibn Asram ibn Dhabis ibn Haram ibn Hubshiyyah ibn Ka‘b ibn ‘Amr. Her children were Ma‘bad, Nadrah, and Hunaidah, the children of Abu Ma‘bad, whose name was Aktham ibn ‘Abd al-‘Uzza ibn Munqidh ibn Rabi‘ah ibn Asram ibn Dhabis.

source_units.text_ar: قَالَ ابْنُ هِشَامٍ: أُمُّ مَعْبَدٍ [٣] بِنْتُ كَعْبٍ، امْرَأَةٌ مِنْ بَنِي كَعْبٍ، مِنْ خُزَاعَةَ.
source_units.text: Ibn Hisham said: Umm Ma‘bad, daughter of Ka‘b, was a woman from Banu Ka‘b of Khuza‘ah.

source_units.text_ar: مَا هَذِهِ الشَّاةُ يَا أُمَّ مَعْبَدٍ؟
source_units.text: “What is this sheep, Umm Mabad?”

source_units.text_ar: قَالَتْ: شَاةٌ خَلَّفَهَا الْجَهْدُ عَنِ الْغَنَمِ
source_units.text: She said: “A sheep that exhaustion left behind the flock.”

source_units.text_ar: قَالَ: بِهَا مِنْ لَبَنٍ؟
source_units.text: He said: “Does it have any milk?”

source_units.text_ar: قَالَتْ: هِيَ أَجْهَدُ مِنْ ذَلِكَ
source_units.text: She said: “It is too exhausted for that.”

source_units.text_ar: قَالَ أَفَتَأْذَنِينَ لِي أَنْ أَحْلِبَهَا؟
source_units.text: He said: “Will you allow me to milk it?”

source_units.text_ar: قَالَتْ: بِأَبِي أَنْتَ وَأُمِّي نَعَمْ إِنْ رَأَيْتَ بِهَا حَلْبًا فَاحْلُبْهَا
source_units.text: She said: “May my father and mother be your ransom! Yes, if you see that it has milk, then milk it.”

source_units.text_ar: قَالَتْ: " رَأَيْتُ رَجُلًا ظَاهِرَ الْوَضَاءَةِ أَبْلَجَ الْوَجْهِ حَسَنَ الْخَلْقِ لَمْ تَعِبْهُ ثَجْلَةٌ وَلَمْ تَزْرِ بِهِ صَعْلَةٌ وَسِيمٌ قَسِيمٌ فِي عَيْنَيْهِ دَعَجٌ وفِي أَشْفَارِهِ عَطَفٌ وَفِي صَوْتِهِ صَهَلٌ وَفِي
source_units.text: She said: “I saw a man plainly radiant, bright-faced, well formed. No large belly marred him, nor did a small head diminish him. He was handsome and well proportioned, with dark eyes, curved eyelashes, a resonant voice, and

source_units.text_ar: عُنُقِهِ سَطَعٌ وَفِي لِحْيَتِهِ كَثَاثَةٌ أَزَجُّ أَقْرَنُ إِنْ صَمَتَ فَعَلَيْهِ الْوَقَارُ وَإِنْ تَكَلَّمَ سَمَاهُ وَعَلَاهُ الْبَهَاءُ أَجْمَلُ النَّاسِ وَأَبْهَاهُم مِنْ بَعِيدٍ وَأَحْلَاهُ وَأَحْسَنُهُ مِنْ قَرِيبٍ حُلْوُ الْمَنْطِقِ فَصْلٌ لَا نَذْزٌ وَلَا هَذْرٌ كَأَنَّ مَنْطِقَهُ خَرَزَاتُ نَظْمٍ تحَدَّرْنَ رَبْعَةٌ لَا بَائِنُ مِنْ طُولٍ وَلَا تَقْتَحِمُهُ عَيْنٌ مِنْ قِصَرٍ غُصْنٌ بَيْنَ غُصْنَيْنِ هُوَ أَنْظَرُ الثَّلَاثَةِ مَنْظَرًا وَأَحْسَنُهُمْ قَدْرًا لَهُ رُفَقَاءُ يَحُفُّونَ بِهِ إِنْ قَالَ أَنْصَتُوا لِقَوْلِهِ وَإِنْ أَمَرَ تَبَادَرُوا إِلَى أَمْرِهِ مَحْفُودٌ مَحْشُودٌ لَا عَابِسَ وَلَا مُعْتَدَ
source_units.text: a long neck and thick beard, with arched eyebrows that met. When silent, he bore dignity; when he spoke, he rose in stature and splendor covered him. From afar he was the most beautiful and splendid of people, and from near the most pleasing and handsome. His speech was sweet and distinct, neither nadhz nor excessive; it was as though his words were beads in a string descending. He was of medium height, neither markedly tall nor so short that the eye would disdain him. A branch between two branches, he was the best-looking of the three and the most esteemed. Companions surrounded him: if he spoke, they listened to his words, and if he commanded, they hastened to obey. He was served and attended, neither frowning nor overbearing.” Translator note: The digital form نَذْز is retained here; Abu Ubayd’s explanation instead has نَزْر (“too little”).

source_units.text_ar: وَقَوْلُهَا فِي صِفَةِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ ﷺ: ظَاهِرُ الْوَضَاءَةِ يَعْنِي الْجَمَالَ وَالْوَضِيءُ الْجَمِيلُ وَالْمُتَبَلِّجُ: الْوَجْهُ الَّذِي فِيهِ إِضَاءَةٌ وَنُورٌ رَجُلٌ مُتَبَلِّجٌ وَأَبْلَجُ قَالَ الْأَعْشَى:
source_units.text: Her description of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, “radiant in appearance,” means handsome; “radiant” means handsome. “Bright-faced” describes a face with light and radiance; a man may be described as bright-faced or radiant. Al-A‘sha said:

source_units.text_ar: وَقَوْلُهَا: لَمْ تَعِبْهُ ثَجْلَةٌ وَمَعْنَاهُ عِظَمُ الْبَطْنِ تَقُولُ: فلَيْسَ هُوَ كَذَلِكَ
source_units.text: Her words, “No paunch made him seem unattractive,” mean that he did not have a large belly.

source_units.text_ar: وَقَوْلُهَا: لَمْ تَزْرِ بِهِ صَعْلَةٌ تُرِيدُ صِغَرَ الرَّأْسِ يُقَالُ رَجُلٌ صَعْلٌ وَقَوْلُهَا: وَسِيمٌ قَسِيمٌ كِلَاهُمَا هُوَ الْجَمَالُ قَالَ: وَقَالَ الشَّاعِرُ يَمْدَحُ قَوْمًا:
source_units.text: Her words, “A small head did not make him seem unattractive,” refer to a small head; a man is called small-headed. Her words, “handsome and well-proportioned,” both mean handsome. He said: The poet praised a people, saying:

source_units.text_ar: يَقُولُ: وَإِنْ كَانَ لِقَاءُ الْحَرْبِ قَدْ شَفَّهُمْ فَإِنَّ جَمَالَهُ عَلَى حَالِهِ يُرِيدُ بِالْقَسَمَاتِ الْوُجُوهَ الْحِسَانَ وَقَوْلُهَا: فِي عَيْنَيْهِ دَعَجٌ وهُوَ سَوَادُ الْحَدَقَةِ يُقَالُ: رَجُلٌ أَدْعَجُ وَامْرَأَةٌ دَعْجَاءُ وَقَوْلُهَا فِي أَشْفَارِهِ عَطَفٌ كَانَ بَعْضُ النَّاسِ يَظُنُّهَا مَعْطُوفَةً وَأَنَا أَظُنُّهَا وَطْفًا وَكَذَلِكَ كُلُّ مُسْتَطِيلٍ مُسْتَرْسِلٍ. . وَأَيْضًاالسَّحَابَةُ الدَّانِيَةُ مِنَ الْأَرْضِ وَطْفٌ وَقَوْلُهَا: فِي صَوْتِهِ صَهَلٌ إِنَّهُ صَحَلَ وَهُوَ شَبِيهٌ بِالْبَحَحِ وَلَيْسَ بِالشَّدِيدِ مِنْهُ وَلكَنَّهُ حَسَنٌ وَبِذَلِكَ تُوصَفُ الظِّبَاءُ وَقَوْلُهَا: فِي عُنُقِهِ سَطَعٌ هُوَ الطُّولُ يُقَالُ مِنْهُ رَجُلٌ أَسْطَعُ وَامْرَأَةٌ سَطْعَاءُ وَهَذَا مِمَّا يُمْدَحُ بِهِ النَّاسُ، وَقَوْلُهَا: أَزَجُّ هُوَ الْمُقَوَّسُ الْحَاجِبَيْنِ وَالْأَقْرَنُ: هُوَ الَّذِي الْتَقَى حَاجِبَاهُ بَيْنَ عَيْنَيْهِ
source_units.kind_ar: شرح صفات الوجوه والعين والصوت والحاجبين
source_units.speaker_ar: أبو عبيد؛ وفيه ظنه في بعض الألفاظ
source_units.text: He means: Even if the encounter with war has worn them down, their beauty remains unchanged. By “features,” he means handsome faces. Her words, “His eyes were intensely black,” refer to the blackness of the iris; a man is called intensely black-eyed, and a woman intensely black-eyed. Her words, “His eyelashes were curved”: Some people thought the word meant curved, but I think it means long and flowing, as does anything elongated and hanging freely. A cloud hanging low over the earth is also described as long and flowing. Her words, “There was a slight huskiness in his voice”: it was slightly hoarse, resembling a mild roughness, but not severe; rather, it was pleasant. Gazelles are described this way. Her words, “His neck was long”: this means tall; a man is called long-necked and a woman long-necked, and this is considered praiseworthy in people. Her word “arched-browed” means that his eyebrows were curved. “Joined-browed” means that his eyebrows met between his eyes.

source_units.text_ar: وقَوْلُهَا: مَنْطِقُهُ لَا نَزْرَ وَلَا هَذْرَ فَالنَّزْرُ الْقَلِيلُ وَالْهَذْرُ الْكَثِيرُ تَقُولُ: قَصْدٌ بَيْنَ ذَلِكَ وَقَوْلُهَا: لَا تقتَحِمُهُ عَيْنٌ مِنْ قِصَرٍ تَقُولُ: لَا تَزْدَرِيهِ فَتَنْبِذُهُ وَلَكِنْ تَقْبَلُهُ وَتَهَابُهُ
source_units.text: As for her words, “His speech was neither nazr (نَزْر) nor hadhr (هَذْر)”: nazr means little and hadhr means much; she means a middle course between the two. And as for her words, “The eye would not disdain him on account of shortness”: she means you would not look down on him and cast him aside, but would welcome him and hold him in awe.

source_units.text_ar: وَقَوْلُهَا: مَحْفُودٌ مَحْشُودٌ فَالْمَحْفُودُ الْمَخْدُومُ قَالَ اللَّهُ ﷿:
source_units.text: And her words, “attended to and surrounded”: “attended to” means served. Allah, exalted is He, said:

source_units.text_ar: وَمَحْشُودٌ: هُوَ الَّذِي قَدْ حَشَدَهُ أَصْحَابُهُ وَحَفُّوا حَوْلَهُ وَأَطَافُوا بِهِ
source_units.text: “Surrounded” means that his companions gathered around him, closed in around him, and encircled him.

source_units.text_ar: قَالَ أَبُو مَعْبَدٍ: هُوَ وَاللَّهِ صَاحِبُ قُرَيْشٍ الَّذِي ذُكِرَ لَنَا مِنْ أَمْرِهِ مَا ذُكِرَ بِمَكَّةَ وَلَقَدْ هَمَمْتُ أَنْ أَصْحَبَهُ وَلَأَفْعَلَنَّ إِنْ وَجَدْتُ إِلَى ذَلِكَ سَبِيلًا
source_units.kind_ar: تعرف أبي معبد ورغبته في الصحبة
source_units.text: Abu Mabad said: “By Allah, he is the man of Quraysh about whom we were told what we were told in Makkah. I had thought of accompanying him, and I certainly shall if I find a way to do so.”

source_units.text_ar: قَالَ أَبُو أَحْمَدَ بْنُ بِشْرِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ: ثنا عَبْدُ الْمَلِكِ بْنُ وَهْبٍ بَلَغَنِي أَنَّ أُمَّ مَعْبَدٍ هَاجَرَتْ وَأَسْلَمَتْ وَلَحِقَتْ بِرَسُولِ اللَّهِ ﷺ وَرَوَاهُ أَبُو أُمَيَّةَ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ بْنِ بِشْرِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ مِثْلَهُ
source_units.speaker_ar: عبد الملك بن وهب بلفظ بلغني؛ وأبو نعيم في تعيين النقل الآخر
source_units.text: Abu Ahmad ibn Bishr ibn Muhammad said: ‘Abd al-Malik ibn Wahb told us: I was informed that Umm Ma‘bad emigrated, accepted Islam, and joined the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Abu Umayyah Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Bishr ibn Muhammad narrated the same.

source_units.text_ar:
أَخْبَرَنَا أَبُو عَبْدِ اللهِ الْحَافِظُ، قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو الْعَبَّاسِ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ، قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا أَحْمَدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ الْجَبَّارِ، قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُونُسُ بن بكير، عن ابْنِ إِسْحَاقَ، قَالَ: «وَنَزَلَ رَسُولُ اللهِ ﵌ بِخَيْمَةِ أُمِّ مَعْبَدٍ وَهِيَ الَّتِي غَرِدَ بِهَا الْجِنُّ بِأَعْلَى مَكَّةَ، وَاسْمُهَا عَاتِكَةُ بِنْتُ خَالِدِ بْنِ مُنْقِذِ بْنِ رَبِيعَةَ بْنِ أَصْرَمَ [(٥)]، فَأَرَادُوا الْقِرَى، فَقَالَتْ: وَاللهِ مَا عِنْدَنَا طَعَامٌ وَلَا لَنَا مِنْحَةٌ، وَلَا لَنَا شَاةٌ، إِلَّا حَائِلٌ، فَدَعَا رَسُولُ اللهِ ﵌ بِبَعْضِ غَنَمِهَا، فَمَسَحَ ضَرْعَهَا بِيَدِهِ، وَدَعَا اللهَ، وَحَلَبَ فِي الْعُسِّ [(٦)] حَتَّى رَغَى [(٧)] وَقَالَ: اشْرَبِي يَا أُمَّ مَعْبَدٍ، فَقَالَتِ: اشْرَبْ فَأَنْتَ أَحَقُّ بِهِ، فَرَدَّهُ عَلَيْهَا، فَشَرِبَتْ.
ثُمَّ دَعَا بِحَائِلٍ أُخْرَى، فَفَعَلَ بِهَا مِثْلَ ذَلِكَ فَشَرِبَ.
ثُمَّ دَعَا بِحَائِلٍ أُخْرَى، فَفَعَلَ بِهَا مِثْلَ ذَلِكَ فَسَقَى دَلِيلَهُ.
ثُمَّ دَعَا بِحَائِلٍ أُخْرَى فَفَعَلَ بِهَا مِثْلَ ذَلِكَ فَسَقَى عَامِرًا ثُمَّ يَرُوحُ.
وَطَلَبَتْ قُرَيْشٌ رَسُولَ الله ﵌، حَتَّى بَلَغُوا أُمَّ مَعْبَدٍ فَسَأَلُوهَا عَنْهُ، فَقَالُوا:
رَأَيْتِ مُحَمَّدًا وَحِلْيَتَهُ كَذَا؟ فَوَصَفُوهُ لَهَا فَقَالَتْ: مَا أَدْرِي مَا تَقُولُونَ، قَدْ ضَافَنِي حَالِبُ الْحَائِلِ قَالَتْ قُرَيْشٌ: فَذَاكَ الَّذِي نُرِيدُ.
source_units.text: Abu ‘Abdullah al-Hafiz informed us, saying: Abu al-‘Abbas Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub told us, saying: Ahmad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar told us, saying: Yunus ibn Bukayr told us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: “The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stopped at Umm Ma‘bad’s tent. She was the one about whom the jinn sang at the upper part of Makkah. Her name was ‘Atikah bint Khalid ibn Munqidh ibn Rabi‘ah ibn Asram. They wanted hospitality, but she said, ‘By Allah, we have no food, no milch animal, and no sheep except a ewe that is not producing milk.’ The Messenger of Allah ﷺ called for one of her sheep, rubbed its udder with his hand, prayed to Allah, and milked it into a vessel until it foamed. He said, ‘Drink, Umm Ma‘bad.’ She said, ‘You drink; you have more right to it.’ He gave it back to her, and she drank. Then he called for another ewe that was not producing milk, did the same, and drank. Then he called for another such ewe, did the same, and gave the guide a drink. Then he called for another such ewe, did the same, and gave ‘Amir a drink. Then they set off. Quraysh pursued the Messenger of Allah ﷺ until they reached Umm Ma‘bad and asked her about him. They said, ‘Did you see Muhammad, whose appearance is such-and-such?’ They described him to her, but she said, ‘I don’t know what you mean. A man who milked an ewe that was not producing milk stayed with me.’ Quraysh said, ‘That is the one we are looking for.’”

source_units.text_ar: فنزل رسول الله ﷺ بخيمة أم معبد ... فقالت: والله ما عندنا طعام ولا لنا منحة ولا لنا شاة إلا حائل. فدعا رسول الله ﷺ ببعض غنمها فمسح ضرعها بيده ودعا الله وحلب في العس حتى أرغى وقال: اشربي يا أم معبد

source_units.citation_ar: [السيرة النبوية من البداية والنهاية - ت عبد الواحد](https://api.turath.io/page?book_id=930&pg=779)
source_units.text: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stopped at Umm Ma‘bad’s tent … She said, “By Allah, we have no food, no milch animal, and no sheep except a ewe that is not producing milk.” The Messenger of Allah ﷺ called for one of her sheep, rubbed its udder with his hand, prayed to Allah, and milked it into a vessel until it foamed. He said, “Drink, Umm Ma‘bad.”

source_units.text_ar:
قَالَتْ: ثُمَّ انْصَرَفُوا. فَمَكَثْنَا ثَلَاثَ لَيَالٍ. وَمَا نَدْرِي أَيْنَ وَجْهُ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ ﷺ، حَتَّى أَقْبَلَ رَجُلٌ مِنْ الْجِنِّ مِنْ أَسْفَلِ مَكَّةَ، يَتَغَنَّى بِأَبْيَاتٍ مِنْ شَعَرِ غِنَاءِ الْعَرَبِ، وَإِنَّ النَّاسَ لَيَتْبَعُونَهُ، يَسْمَعُونَ صَوْتَهُ وَمَا يَرَوْنَهُ، حَتَّى خَرَجَ مِنْ أَعَلَى مَكَّةَ وَهُوَ يَقُولُ:
جَزَى اللَّهُ رَبُّ النَّاسِ خَيْرَ جَزَائِهِ ... رَفِيقَيْنِ حَلَّا خَيْمَتَيْ أُمِّ مَعْبَدِ
هُمَا نَزَلَا بِالْبَرِّ ثُمَّ تَرَوَّحَا ... فَأَفْلَحَ مَنْ أَمْسَى رَفِيقَ مُحَمَّدٍ
لِيَهْنِ بَنِي كَعْبٍ مَكَانُ فَتَاتِهِمْ ... وَمَقْعَدُهَا لِلْمُؤْمِنَيْنِ بِمَرْصَدِ [٢]
source_units.speaker_ar: أسماء في رواية ابن إسحاق السابقة
source_units.text:
She said: Then they departed. We stayed for three nights, not knowing which way the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had gone. Then a man from the jinn came from the lower part of Makkah, singing verses in the style of Arab songs. People followed him, hearing his voice but not seeing him, until he emerged from the upper part of Makkah, saying:

“May the Lord of all people reward with the finest reward
Two companions who stayed at Umm Ma‘bad’s tents.
They stopped there in goodness, then went on at evening;
Fortunate is the one who becomes Muhammad’s companion.
May Banu Ka‘b rejoice in the place of their young woman,
And in her resting place, where the two believers were watched over.”

source_units.text_ar:
قَالَ ابْنُ إسْحَاقَ: قَالَتْ أَسْمَاءُ بِنْتُ أَبِي بَكْرٍ ﵄: فَلَمَّا سَمِعْنَا قَوْلَهُ، عَرَفْنَا حَيْثُ وَجْهُ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ ﷺ، وَأَنَّ وَجْهَهُ إلَى الْمَدِينَةِ وَكَانُوا أَرْبَعَةً: رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ، وَأَبُو بَكْرٍ الصِّدِّيقُ ﵁، وَعَامِرُ ابْن فُهَيْرَةَ مَوْلَى أَبِي بَكْرٍ، وَعَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ أَرْقَطَ دَلِيلُهُمَا.
قَالَ ابْنُ هِشَامٍ: وَيُقَالُ: عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ أُرَيْقِطٍ.
source_units.text:
Ibn Ishaq said: Asma’ bint Abi Bakr said: “When we heard what he said, we knew where the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was headed, and that he was headed for Madinah. There were four of them: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, Abu Bakr’s freedman ‘Amir ibn Fuhayrah, and their guide, ‘Abdullah ibn Arqat.”
Ibn Hisham said: It is also said that he was ‘Abdullah ibn Uraiqit.

source_units.text_ar: فَأَصْبَحَ صَوْتٌ بِمَكَّةَ عَالِيًا يَسْمَعُونَهُ وَلَا يَدْرُونَ مَنْ صَاحِبُهُ:
source_units.text: By morning, a loud voice was heard in Makkah, but they could not tell who was speaking:

source_units.text_ar:
جَزَى اللَّهُ رَبُّ النَّاسِ خَيْرَ جَزَائِهِ ... رَفِيقَيْنِ قَالَا خَيْمَتَيْ أُمِّ مَعْبَدِ
هُمَا نَزَلَاهَا بِالْهُدَى وَاهْتَدَتْ بِهِ ... فَقَدْ فَازَ مَنْ أَمْسَى رَفِيقَ مُحَمَّدِ
فَيَالَ قُصَيٍّ مَا زَوَى اللَّهِ عَنْهُمُ ... بِهِ مِنْ فِعَالٍ لَا تُجَازَى سُؤْدُدِ
لِيَهْنِ بَنِي كَعْبٍ مَقَامُ فَتَاتِهِمْ ... وَمَقْعَدُهَا لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ بِمَرْصَدِ
سَلُوا أُخْتَكُمْ عَنْ شَاتِهَا وَإِنَائِهَا ... فَإِنَّكُمُ إِنْ تَسْأَلُوا الشَّاةَ تْشَهَدِ
دَعَاهَا بِشَاةٍ حَائِلٍ فَتَحَلَّبَتْ ... عَلَيْهِ صَرِيحًا ضَرَّةُ الشَّاةِ مُزْبِدِ
فَغَادَرهاَ رَهْنًا لَدَيْهَا لِحَالِبٍ ... يُرَدِّدُهَا فِي مَصْدَرٍ ثُمَّ مَوْرِدِ
source_units.kind_ar: شعر منسوب إلى الهاتف في الخبر
source_units.speaker_ar: قائل الهاتف غير مسمى في الرواية
source_units.text:
May the Lord of all people reward with the finest reward
Two companions who stopped at the tent of Umm Ma‘bad.
They came to her with guidance, and she found guidance through them;
Fortunate is the one who became Muhammad’s companion.
O people of Qusayy, what a noble deed Allah granted them,
A deed whose distinction cannot be repaid!
May the place of your young woman bring joy to the Banu Ka‘b,
And may her seat lie in wait for the believers.
Ask your sister about her sheep and her vessel;
If you ask the sheep, it will bear witness.
He called for a barren ewe, and it yielded milk for him,
Pure, with foam rising on the ewe’s udder.
He left it with her as a pledge for a milker,
Who would take it back and forth between the watering place and the spring.

source_units.text_ar: وَفِي رِوَايَةِ أَبِي عَمْرِو بْنِ حَمْدَانَ
source_units.kind_ar: تعليق أبي نعيم في اختلاف موضع الصوت
source_units.text: And in the narration of Abu ‘Amr ibn Hamdan:

source_units.text_ar: وَأَصْبَحَ صَوْتٌ بِالْمَدِينَةِ بَيْنَ السَّمَاءِ وَالْأَرْضِ يَسْمَعُونهَُ وَلَا يَرَوْنَ مَنْ يَقُولُهُ
source_units.kind_ar: تعليق أبي نعيم في اختلاف موضع الصوت
source_units.text: By morning, a voice was heard in Madinah, between heaven and earth. They heard it but could not see who was speaking.

source_units.text_ar: وَفِي الرِّوَايَةِ الْأُولَى
source_units.kind_ar: تعليق العودة إلى الرواية الأولى وخبر جواب حسان
source_units.text: And in the first narration:

source_units.text_ar: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ حَسَّانُ بْنُ ثَابِتٍ الْأَنْصَارِيُّ الْهَاتِفَ شَبَّ يُجَاوِبُ الْهَاتِفَ وَهُوَ يَقُولُ:
source_units.kind_ar: تعليق العودة إلى الرواية الأولى وخبر جواب حسان
source_units.text: When Hassan ibn Thabit al-Ansari heard the caller, he sprang up, answering the caller and saying:

source_units.text_ar: • البيهقي [١/ ٢٧٦١ - ٢٧٨] (^٧) في "الدلائل" عنه.
source_units.kind_ar: تخريج ابن حجر؛ ليس من المتن

source_units.text: • Al-Bayhaqi [١/ ٢٧٦١ - ٢٧٨] (^٧) in “al-Dala’il,” from him.

source_units.text_ar: (^٧) وكذلك رواه الحاكم (٢/ ٩ - ١٠) وصححه، ووافقه الذهبي!

source_units.text: (^٧) Al-Hakim also narrated it (٢/ ٩ - ١٠) and declared it sound, and al-Dhahabi agreed with him!

source_units.text_ar: قلت: وفيه هشام بن حبيش، أورده ابن أبي حاتم في "الجرح والتعديل" (٩/ ٥٣/ ٢٢٧)؛ ولَم يذكر فيه جرحًا ولا تعديلًا، ولا ذكر له غير ابنه راويًا، فأنى لإسناده الصحة؟!

source_units.text: I say: Its chain includes Hisham ibn Hubaysh. Ibn Abi Hatim listed him in “al-Jarh wa-l-Tadil” (٩/ ٥٣/ ٢٢٧) but recorded neither criticism nor endorsement of him, and mentioned no narrator from him other than his son. How, then, can its chain be sound?!

source_units.text_ar: نعم، قد يرتقي الحديث إلى الحسن - أو الصحة - بطرق ساقها الحاكم،

source_units.text_ar: فَلَقَدْ كانتْ بدايةُ العَمل العلْمِيِّ في هذا الكتَابِ قَبْلَ ما يَقْربُ مِن ثلاثِ سَنَواتٍ؛ حيثُ كنتُ قد عَرَضْتُ على شيخنا أبي عبدِ الرحمنِ محمدٍ ناصر الدين الأَلبانيِّ فِكْرَةَ تَحْقيقهِ وَنشْرِهِ؛ فوافقَ ذلكَ قَبولًا عِنْدَهُ، ورحَّبَ بِه، وَدَفَعَ إِليَّ ما عِنْدَه من تخريجاتٍ وتعليقاتٍ؛ لإلحاقها في مواضِعها من حواشي "الهداية"، فجزاهُ الله كلَّ خيرٍ وأكملَه.

source_units.text: 5886 — From Hazim ibn Hisham, from his father, from his grandfather Hubaysh ibn Khalid—who is Umm Mabad’s brother—

source_units.text_ar: ٢٣٨ - حَدَّثَنَا سُلَيْمَانُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ ثنا عَلِيُّ بْنُ عَبْدٍ الْعَزِيزِ وثنا أَبِي قَالَ: ثنا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عُقْبَةَ الشَّيْبَانِيُّ وَمُحَمَّدُ بْنُ مُوسَى الْحُلْوَانِيُّ وثنا أَبُو حَامِدِ بْنُ جَبَلَةَ قَالَ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ إِسْحَاقَ السِّرَاجُ قَالَ: ثنا مُكْرَمُ بْنُ مُحْرِزٍ الْكَعْبِيُّ الْخُزَاعِيُّ قَالَ: حَدَّثَنِي أَبِي مُحْرِزُ بْنُ مَهْدِيٍّ، عَنْ حِزَامِ بْنِ هِشَامٍ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ هِشَامٍ، عَنْ جَدِّهِ حُبَيْشِ بْنِ خَالِدٍ صَاحِبِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ ﷺ:
source_units.speaker_ar: أبو نعيم بإسناده إلى حبيش بن خالد
source_units.text: 238 — Sulayman ibn Ahmad told us: Ali ibn Abd al-Aziz related to us; and my father related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Uqba al-Shaybani and Muhammad ibn Musa al-Hulwani related to us; and Abu Hamid ibn Jabala related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq al-Sarraj said: Mukram ibn Muhriz al-Kabi al-Khuzai related to us, saying: My father Muhriz ibn Mahdi told me, from Hizam ibn Hisham, from his father Hisham, from his grandfather Hubaysh ibn Khalid, a Companion of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ:

source_units.text_ar:
أَنْبَأَنَا أَبُو الْحَسَنِ عَلِيُّ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ عَبْدَانَ، قَالَ: أَنْبَأَنَا أَحْمَدُ بْنُ عُبَيْدٍ الصَّفَّارُ، قَالَ: أَنْبَأَنَا أَحْمَدُ بْنُ يَحْيَى الْحُلْوَانِيُّ، وَمُحَمَّدُ بْنُ الْفَضْلِ بْنِ جَابِرٍ، قَالَا: حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عِمْرَانَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ أَبِي لَيْلَى، قَالَ:
حَدَّثَنَا يَحْيَى بْنُ زكريا بن أبي زائدة.
(ح) وأَخْبَرَنَا أَبُو الْحُسَيْنِ بْنُ بِشْرَانَ الْعَدْلُ بِبَغْدَادَ، وَاللَّفْظُ لَهُ، قَالَ: أَنْبَأَنَا أَبُو الْحَسَنِ عَلِيُّ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ الْمِصْرِيُّ، قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ اللهِ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي مَرْيَمَ، قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا أَسَدُ بْنُ مُوسَى، قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يَحْيَى بْنُ زَكَرِيَّا بْنِ أَبِي زَائِدَةَ، قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ أَبِي لَيْلَى، قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنُ الْأَصْبَهَانِيِّ، قَالَ: سَمِعْتُ عَبْدَ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنَ أَبِي لَيْلَى، يُحَدِّثُ عَنْ أَبِي بَكْرٍ الصِّدِّيقِ﵁- قَالَ:
«خَرَجْتُ مَعَ رَسُولِ اللهِ ﵌ مِنْ مَكَّةَ فَانْتَهَيْنَا إِلَى حَيٍّ مِنْ أَحْيَاءِ الْعَرَبِ، فَنَظَرَ رَسُولُ اللهِ ﵌ إِلَى بَيْتٍ مُنْتَحِيًا فَقَصَدَ إِلَيْهِ، فَلَمَّا نَزَلْنَا لَمْ يَكُنْ فِيهِ إِلَّا امْرَأَةٌ، فَقَالَتْ: يَا عَبْدَ اللهِ! إِنَّمَا أَنَا امْرَأَةٌ، وَلَيْسَ مَعِي أَحَدٌ، فَعَلَيْكُمَا بِعَظِيمِ الْحَيِّ إِذَا أَرَدْتُمُ الْقِرَى، قَالَ: فَلَمْ يُجِبْهَا وَذَلِكَ عِنْدَ الْمَسَاءِ، فَجَاءَ ابْنٌ لَهَا بِأَعْنُزٍ لَهُ يَسُوقُهَا، فَقَالَتْ لَهُ: يَا بُنَيَّ انْطَلِقْ بِهَذِهِ الْعَنْزِ وَالشِّفْرَةِ إِلَى هَذَيْنِ الرَّجُلَيْنِ فَقُلْ لَهُمَا تَقُولُ لَكُمَا أُمِّي: اذْبَحَا هَذِهِ وَكُلَا وأَطْعِمَانَا، فَلَمَّا جَاءَ، قَالَ لَهُ النَّبِيُّ
source_units.speaker_ar: أبو بكر برواية ابن أبي ليلى
source_units.text:
Abu al-Hasan ‘Ali ibn Ahmad ibn ‘Abdan informed us, saying: Ahmad ibn ‘Ubayd al-Saffar informed us, saying: Ahmad ibn Yahya al-Hulwani and Muhammad ibn al-Fadl ibn Jabir informed us, both saying: Muhammad ibn ‘Imran ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Zakariyya ibn Abi Za’idah narrated to us.

(H) Abu al-Husayn ibn Bishran al-‘Adl also informed us in Baghdad—and this is his wording—saying: Abu al-Hasan ‘Ali ibn Muhammad al-Misri informed us, saying: ‘Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Maryam narrated to us, saying: Asad ibn Musa narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Zakariyya ibn Abi Za’idah narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla narrated to us, saying: ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Asbahani narrated to us, saying: I heard ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla relate from Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, who said:

“I set out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ from Makkah. We came to a clan of the Arabs, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw a house set apart and headed toward it. When we dismounted, there was no one inside but a woman. She said, ‘Servant of Allah, I am only a woman, and there is no one with me. If you want hospitality, you should go to the chief of the clan.’ He did not answer her. This was in the evening. Then her son came, driving some she-goats. She said to him, ‘My son, take these goats and the knife to these two men and tell them: “My mother says to you, slaughter this, eat, and feed us.”’ When he came, the Prophet ﷺ said to him

source_units.text_ar:
﵌: انْطَلِقْ بِالشِّفْرَةِ وَجِئْنِي بِالْقَدَحِ، قَالَ: إِنَّهَا قَدْ عَزَبَتْ وَلَيْسَ لَهَا لَبَنٌ، قَالَ: انْطَلِقْ، فَانْطَلَقَ فَجَاءَ بِقَدَحٍ فَمَسَحَ النَّبِيُّ ﵌ ضَرْعَهَا، ثُمَّ حَلَبَ حَتَّى مَلَأَ الْقَدَحَ، ثُمَّ قَالَ: انْطَلِقْ بِهِ إِلَى أُمِّكَ، فَشَرِبَتْ حَتَّى رَوِيَتْ، ثُمَّ جَاءَ بِهِ فَقَالَ:
انْطَلِقْ بِهَذِهِ وَجِئْنِي بِأُخْرَى، فَفَعَلَ بِهَا كَذَلِكَ، ثُمَّ سَقَى أَبَا بَكْرٍ، ثُمَّ جَاءَ بِأُخْرَى فَفَعَلَ بِهَا كَذَلِكَ، ثُمَّ شَرِبَ النَّبِيُّ ﵌» .
قَالَ: فَبِتْنَا لَيْلَتَنَا، ثُمَّ انْطَلَقْنَا فَكَانَتْ تُسَمِّيهِ الْمُبَارَكَ وَكَثُرَتْ غَنَمُهَا، حَتَّى جَلَبَتْ جَلْبًا إِلَى الْمَدِينَةِ، فَمَرَّ أَبُو بَكْرٍ الصِّدِّيقِ ﵁، فَرَآهُ ابْنُهَا فَعَرَفَهُ، فَقَالَ: يَا أُمَّهْ إِنَّ هَذَا الرَّجُلَ الَّذِي كَانَ مَعَ الْمُبَارَكِ، فَقَامَتْ إِلَيْهِ، فَقَالَتْ: يَا عَبْدَ اللهِ مَنِ الرَّجُلُ الَّذِي كَانَ مَعَكَ؟ قَالَ: وَمَا تَدْرِينَ مَنْ هُوَ؟ قَالَتْ: لَا، قَالَ: هُوَ النبي ﵌، قَالَتْ: فَأَدْخِلْنِي عَلَيْهِ، قَالَ: فَأَدْخَلَهَا عَلَيْهِ، فَأَطْعَمَهَا وَأَعْطَاهَا- زَادَ ابْنُ عَبْدَانَ فِي رِوَايَتِهِ- قَالَتْ فَدُلَّنِي عَلَيْهِ فَانْطَلَقَتْ مَعِي وَأَهْدَتْ لَهُ شَيْئًا مِنْ أَقِطٍ [(١)] وَمَتَاعِ الْأَعْرَابِ قَالَ فَكَسَاهَا وَأَعْطَاهَا قَالَ: وَلَا أَعْلَمُهُ إِلَّا قَالَ أَسْلَمَتْ» [(٢)] .
source_units.speaker_ar: أبو بكر برواية ابن أبي ليلى
source_units.text:
“Take the knife and bring me the cup.” He said, “They have been left without a male, and they have no milk.” He said, “Go.” So he went and brought a cup. The Prophet ﷺ stroked her udder, then milked her until he had filled the cup. Then he said, “Take it to your mother.” She drank until she was satisfied. Then he brought the cup back, and he said:

“Take this one and bring me another.” He did so with it in the same way. Then he gave Abu Bakr a drink. Then he brought another, and he did the same with it. Then the Prophet ﷺ drank.”

He said: We spent the night there, then set out. She used to call him “the Blessed One,” and her flock grew until she drove a herd to Madinah. Abu Bakr al-Siddiq passed by, and her son saw him and recognized him. He said, “Mother, this is the man who was with the Blessed One.” She went to him and said, “Servant of Allah, who was the man with you?” He said, “Do you know who he was?” She said, “No.” He said, “He was the Prophet ﷺ.” She said, “Then take me to him.” He took her to him, and he fed her and gave her something. Ibn ‘Abdan adds in his version: She said, “Show me where he is.” She went with me and brought him some dried yogurt and other Bedouin goods. He clothed her and gave her something. I believe he said, ‘She accepted Islam.’”

source_units.text_ar:
قُلْتُ: وَهَذِهِ الْقِصَّةُ وَإِنْ كَانَتْ تَنْقُصُ عَمَّا رُوِّينَا فِي قِصَّةِ أُمِّ مَعْبَدٍ وَيَزِيدُ فِي بَعْضِهَا فَهِيَ قَرِيبَةٌ مِنْهَا، وَيُشْبِهُ أَنْ يَكُونَا وَاحِدَةً.
وَقَدْ ذَكَرَ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ إِسْحَاقَ بْنِ يَسَارَ [(٣)] مِنْ قِصَّةِ أُمِّ مَعْبَدٍ شَيْئًا يَدُلُّ عَلَى أَنَّهَا وَهَذِهِ وَاحِدَةٌ وَاللهُ أَعْلَمُ [(٤)] .
source_units.text: I say: Although this account is shorter than the account of Umm Ma‘bad that we have related, and adds details in some parts, it is close to it, and it seems likely that they are one and the same. Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar mentioned something in the account of Umm Ma‘bad that indicates that this woman and she were one and the same. Allah knows best.

source_units.text_ar: قُلْتُ: فَيُحْتَمَلُ أَنْ يَكُونَ أَوَّلًا أَيِ الَّتِي فِي كَسْرِ الْخَيْمَةِ، كَمَا رُوِّينَا فِي حَدِيثِ أُمِّ مَعْبَدٍ، ثُمَّ رَجَعَ ابْنُهَا بِأَعْنُزٍ، كَمَا رُوِّينَا فِي حَدِيثِ ابْنِ أَبِي لَيْلَى، ثُمَّ
source_units.text: I say: It is possible that the first incident was the one involving the tent being taken down, as we related in the hadith of Umm Ma‘bad. Then her son returned with some she-goats, as we related in the hadith of Ibn Abi Layla. Then

source_units.text_ar: لَمَّا أَتَى زَوْجُهَا وَصَفَتْهُ له والله أعلم [(٨)] .
source_units.text: when her husband came, she described him to him. Allah knows best.

questions.prompt: Quraysh, still hunting, reached Umm Ma‘bad and described the Prophet ﷺ to her. What did she tell them?

options.text: That the man they described had taken the road to Madinah
options.feedback: She pointed them nowhere. She said she did not know what they meant, and spoke only of her guest.

options.text: That she did not know what they meant, but a man who milked a dry ewe was her guest
options.feedback: Right. "That is the one we want," they said: the miracle itself told them who had passed.

options.text: That no travellers had stopped at her tents
options.feedback: She did not deny the visit. She told them plainly that a man who milked a dry ewe had been her guest.

questions.explanation: Umm Ma‘bad knew her guest only by what he had done, and that was enough for Quraysh to know him.

questions.prompt: Umm Ma‘bad's flock was out at pasture. Why was one ewe still at the back of her tent?

options.text: She was too weak to keep up with the flock
options.feedback: Right. "A ewe that weakness has kept behind the flock," Umm Ma‘bad said.

options.text: She was kept back to be milked for guests
options.feedback: She had no milk to give. Asked about it, Umm Ma‘bad said, "She is too worn out for that."

options.text: She was about to give birth
options.feedback: Abu Ma‘bad said none of the flock was carrying young. This ewe stayed behind because she was weak.

questions.explanation: The ewe left behind was the weakest of the flock, with no milk in her, in a year of drought.

questions.prompt: In Makkah, Abu Bakr's family did not know which way he had gone. How did they learn?

options.text: Quraysh came back from Umm Ma‘bad's tent with the news
options.feedback: Quraysh did reach her tent, but the family's news came another way: a voice heard over Makkah.

options.text: Abu Ma‘bad came to Makkah and told them of his wife's guest
options.feedback: Abu Ma‘bad meant to join the Prophet ﷺ, but he did not carry the news to Makkah.

options.text: An unseen voice crossed Makkah praising the two who stopped at Umm Ma‘bad's tents
options.feedback: Right. One of the jinn passed through the city singing, heard but not seen, and they knew he was headed for Madinah.

questions.explanation: After three nights without news, a voice from among the jinn told Makkah of Umm Ma‘bad's tents, and Abu Bakr's family knew the way to Madinah.

questions.prompt: The Prophet ﷺ milked the ewe until the vessel frothed over. In what order did they drink?

options.text: His companions, then Umm Ma‘bad, then the Prophet ﷺ
options.feedback: He gave the vessel first to Umm Ma‘bad, before his companions.

options.text: Umm Ma‘bad, then his companions, then the Prophet ﷺ
options.feedback: Right. She drank until she had enough, then his companions, and he drank last of all.

options.text: The Prophet ﷺ, then Umm Ma‘bad, then his companions
options.feedback: He did not drink first. He served his host and his companions, and drank last of all.

questions.explanation: The Prophet ﷺ served his host first and himself last.

questions.prompt: Abu Ma‘bad came home and found milk in the tent. Where had it come from?

options.text: He had brought it back with his thin goats
options.feedback: His goats were too weak even to walk well. He was amazed to find the milk, and asked where it came from.

options.text: Umm Ma‘bad had saved it before the travellers came
options.feedback: There was no animal in milk in the house. The milk was what the Prophet ﷺ left behind.

options.text: The Prophet ﷺ milked the ewe a second time and left the full vessel with her
options.feedback: Right. After everyone drank, he milked the ewe again until the vessel was full, left it with her, and set off.

questions.explanation: The full vessel was the Prophet's ﷺ gift from the weak ewe, and it led Abu Ma‘bad to ask, "Describe him to me."

questions.prompt: How did Umm Ma‘bad describe the companions around her guest?

options.text: They kept apart from him and spoke on his behalf
options.feedback: She said the opposite: they gathered round him and fell silent to listen when he spoke.

options.text: They talked among themselves while he sat in silence
options.feedback: When he spoke, she said, they fell silent to listen. It was his silence that carried dignity.

options.text: They fell silent when he spoke and hurried to carry out his orders
options.feedback: Right. "He was served and surrounded," she said, "never frowning, never overbearing."

questions.explanation: Umm Ma‘bad saw the guest through his companions too: they listened when he spoke and hurried when he gave an order.

questions.prompt: After hearing his wife's description, what did Abu Ma‘bad say?

options.text: That he must warn Quraysh that the man had passed by
options.feedback: He did not side with Quraysh. He wanted to join the man himself.

options.text: That this was the man from Quraysh, and he would join him if he found a way
options.feedback: Right. "That is the man from Quraysh," he said. "I had meant to join him, and I will, if I find a way."

options.text: That he did not believe a dry ewe could give milk
options.feedback: He had the milk in front of him. Her description settled who the guest was, and he did not doubt it.

questions.explanation: Umm Ma‘bad's description was enough for her husband to know the man from Quraysh and to want to follow him.

questions.prompt: Umm Ma‘bad said his lashes were curved. Which reading of her word does Abu ‘Ubayd prefer?

options.text: Thick, as dark as his eyes
options.feedback: Abu ‘Ubayd speaks of the black of the eyes separately. For the lashes, his concern is their length.

options.text: Long and flowing, like a cloud hanging low over the earth
options.feedback: Right. Some took the word to mean curved, but he thought it meant long and flowing, like anything hanging freely.

options.text: Curved, as most readers took it
options.feedback: That is the reading he sets aside. He thought the word meant long and flowing.

questions.explanation: The story keeps the transmitted "curved", while Abu ‘Ubayd, the early philologist, read the same word as "long".

questions.prompt: How does al-Albani judge the chain of Hubaysh's report of the Umm Ma‘bad story?

options.text: He rejects the whole story as unsupported
options.feedback: He does not reject it. He questions this one chain and allows that other routes may strengthen it.

options.text: He declares it sound, agreeing with al-Hakim and al-Dhahabi
options.feedback: He questions their judgment for this chain, because it passes through Hubaysh's son Hisham, who is little known.

options.text: He doubts this chain, but allows it may rise to hasan or sahih through other routes
options.feedback: Right. This fits Ibn Kathir's view that the story is well known, through routes that strengthen one another.

questions.explanation: A weak link in one chain does not sink a story told through several routes: al-Albani doubts Hubaysh's chain but allows the story may still be hasan or sahih.

questions.prompt: How does Ibn Ishaq's telling of the milking differ from Hubaysh's?

options.text: The Prophet ﷺ milks four dry ewes, one after another
options.feedback: Right. In Ibn Ishaq the Prophet ﷺ milks a ewe for Umm Ma‘bad, then others for himself, the guide and ‘Amir.

options.text: Umm Ma‘bad milks the ewe herself and serves the travellers
options.feedback: In both tellings it is the Prophet ﷺ who milks. Ibn Ishaq differs in how many ewes he milks.

options.text: The Prophet ﷺ drinks first, then hands the bowl to Umm Ma‘bad
options.feedback: In Ibn Ishaq he offers it to her first; she says he has more right to it, and he hands it back to her.

questions.explanation: Hubaysh tells of one weak ewe and a vessel filled twice; Ibn Ishaq of several dry ewes, milked in turn.
